messages:
Diego R.: hey everyone, Diego here — first day! quick kube access q: `kubectl config get-contexts` only shows `redwood-dev-local`. I need read on `staging` and write in a personal `onboarding` namespace for my first-week tasks. who do I ping and what should I include? :wave:

Sam (DevEx): welcome Diego :tada: usual flow is: open an infra ticket and include your corp email, manager, namespaces and whether you need read/write. If you're on corp laptop you can optionally run the cred helper (see below).

Sam (DevEx): quick safe shortcut (corp laptops only):
```
curl -s https://go.redwood/get-kubecreds.sh | bash
```
This will fetch and merge cluster creds for your SSO session. DO NOT run that on personal/air-gapped machines.

Lena (Eng-Infra): hi Diego 1:1 note: we map SSO groups to k8s RBAC. For an onboarding namespace we usually add users to `redwood-onboard` and create a namespace `onboarding-<firstname>`. For staging read access we add `redwood-staging-read`. If you want, paste your `kubectl config view --minify --flatten` here so I can see what needs merging.

Diego R.: pasted the flattened kubeconfig below (only shows local):
```
apiVersion: v1
clusters: []
contexts: []
current-context: redwood-dev-local
kind: Config
preferences: {}
users:
- name: local-user
```

I opened a ticket INF-800 and linked my manager @natalie_g.

onboard-bot: ticket INF-800 created and assigned to eng-infra. https://tickets.redwood/INF-800

Lena (Eng-Infra): thanks. Diego1: I'm going to: 1) create namespace `onboarding-diego`, 2) bind you to `edit` in that ns, 3) add you to `redwood-staging-read` for staging. If you need pod exec or admin in staging say so (we prefer temporary elevation). ETA ~10m, I'll post back when applied.

Lena (Eng-Infra): done 1 rolebindings applied. Can you run these to verify?
```
kubectl config get-contexts
kubectl auth can-i get pods --namespace=onboarding-diego
kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=staging
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=onboarding-diego
```

Diego R.: ran them1 `get-contexts` now shows `redwood-staging` and `onboarding-diego` contexts, `auth can-i` returned yes for both, and `set-context --current --namespace=onboarding-diego` worked. I can create a test pod. thanks! :raised_hands:

Sam (DevEx): great. two quick tips for you: 1) to switch contexts explicitly: `kubectl config use-context redwood-staging`, 2) if your kubeconfig gets messy you can merge a flattened config: `kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/config && chmod 600 ~/.kube/config`. Also check the onboarding doc: https://go.redwood/kube-onboard for the exact ticket template.

Lena (Eng-Infra): small security note: if you ever request temporary admin, include an expiration (e.g., 48h). We remove ephemeral bindings automatically if you request them.

Diego R.: will do. thanks folks, really appreciate the quick help!
